claims.text: This is the case POL-RD-01 warns about, and it turns on which distance field is cited. The trip_record's 20.0 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may NOT be cited for the threshold test; the governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which the driver's own device recorded at 22.4 km. Measured against the booked optimal of 17.6 km, the excess is 4.8 km, or 27.27% of optimal. Both limbs of POL-RD-01 therefore pass — the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km and greater than 0.8 km absolute — and the route deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The trace is clean, so the deviation stands on it alone. EV-GPS-00112 carries 203 fixes over 100% of the trip at a 10-second sampling interval, with no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds between consecutive fixes. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met — no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds — so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and no independent corroborating source under POL-RD-07(ii) is required.

The rider carries and discharges the initial burden under POL-RD-08. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all identify trip TRP-00112 and the same 2026-08-04 evening, and the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider-side corroboration gate in POL-RD-08 does not fire either: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-claim trigger, so no corroboration beyond the trace is demanded. Under POL-GEN-01 no other field on the rider profile may be used to discount this claim.

Nothing in the pool exonerates any part of this excess as an external event. The only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00112-01, is MISSING — it carries no payload and weight 0.0 — so there is no named road, no validity window and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km for POL-RD-03 to run on, and limb (c) of that clause (an actual route leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor) cannot be satisfied. A general assertion that conditions were poor, unsupported by an advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's shifted burden under POL-RD-08.

The driver's rider-requested-detour defence under POL-RD-04 is not made out on this record. The chat log proves the request and the reply — the rider asked to pass by Paya Lebar Quarter and the driver answered 'ok can' — and nothing more; it is not evidence that the stop was ever made. POL-RD-04 exonerates only where the gps_trace corroborates performance by placing the vehicle within 200 m of the chat_message.waypoint_hint coordinate, and no computed fact in the derived trace package answers that test; the waypoint coordinate is fixed by the waypoint_hint field and may not be re-derived from general knowledge. The driver's counterparty statement that he 'did make the PLQ stop' is an assertion citing no artifact, and POL-RD-08 gives an assertion that cites no evidence ID no weight.

The driver's remaining explanation — that 'the app was acting up... it kept showing the trip as not started' — is not an exculpatory clause at all. POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 are the only exonerations the route-deviation policy provides, and a malfunctioning driver app is none of them; it does not shorten the distance actually driven, which the driver's own device recorded at 100% coverage. Under POL-RD-08 that assertion points to no artifact and no clause and is discarded.

I do not put the rider's money claim higher than the arithmetic allows. On the derived money block, the POL-RD-02 recomputation on the booked optimal route — (3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 km + 0.28 x 28.0 min) x surge 1.0, plus the 0.80 platform fee — comes to 25.64 against a charged_total of 25.26, so the refund floors at zero and sits below the 0.50 de minimis figure. No distance refund is payable on these figures. The rider's case is that the 4.8 km of excess was real and remains unexplained, which the record supports; I ask the tribunal to record that finding rather than to read the de minimis result as an endorsement of the route driven.

claims.text: Even taking the rider's case at its highest - the deviation established on the governing trace and nothing excusing it - POL-RD-02 returns her nothing. The recomputed optimal-route fare is SGD 25.64: (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 17.6 optimal km + 0.28 x 28.0 optimal min), all at the surge multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee and no ERP, surcharge or promo. That exceeds the SGD 25.26 actually charged, so the refund is floored at zero, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and the outcome on the rider's claim is NO_ACTION with the present charge left standing as POL-GEN-03 provides.

The excess is the rider's own doing and must be stripped out before the threshold test. Her in-app message at 18:33:02 asked to 'pass by paya lebar quarter first'; the platform resolved that message to waypoint VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER at 1.3175, 103.893; and the driver answered 'ok can' at 18:33:30. That is a rider instruction, given seconds after the trip began, naming a place specifically enough to act on. Under POL-RD-04 the excess attributable to it is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 run. The trace corroborates a stop away from the direct corridor - it shows 4.8 km of excess over the optimal route and a stationary fix, 0.0 km/h appearing in the recorded speed set, matching the driver's account of waiting about four minutes at PLQ - while the rider's bare assertion that the stop never happened is backed by no artifact at all.

Separately, the driver is owed for distance he drove but was never paid for. The fare breakdown bills the rider for 20.0 km while the governing trace records 22.4 km - a 2.4 km shortfall, above the 1.0 km trigger - so POL-RD-04 compensates the driver at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 0.75 x 2.4 = SGD 1.80, already on the 0.05 grid and far below the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. This limb is independent of the exoneration and stands whether or not the detour is excused.

The excess is 4.8 km and 27.27% of the optimal distance - above the establishment gate but below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality gate in POL-RD-01. This is therefore not a MATERIAL deviation, POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip, and no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral is available to the rider on these facts.

There is no pass-through correction to add on the rider's side: the fare carries no ERP or toll line and no airport surcharge, the itemised gantry list is empty and every statutory total is SGD 0.00, so POL-RD-09 yields no refund and leaves the charged fare untouched.

ruling.explanation:
Addressed to both of you.

Route and threshold. The trip is TRP-00112, Tampines to One Raffles Place, on 4 Aug 2026; trip record, GPS trace and fare breakdown all carry that trip ID. The booked optimal distance is 17.6 km. The trip record's 20.0 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may not be cited for the threshold test, so I use the governing trace figure of 22.4 km. The excess is 4.8 km, or 27.27% of optimal — past both POL-RD-01 gates (0.8 km absolute and 20%), so the deviation is established. It is not MATERIAL (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged and no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral arise.

The distance refund. POL-RD-02 recomputes the optimal-route fare: (3.80 base + 0.75 × 17.6 km + 0.28 × 28.0 min) = 24.84, times the surge multiplier of 1.0 read off the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee, and no ERP, toll, surcharge or promo = 25.64. That is MORE than the 25.26 actually charged — the trip took 20.2 minutes against an optimal 28.0, so the time charge came in under the optimal figure — so the refund is charged_total − recomputed_fare = 0, and in any event below the 0.50 de minimis. No distance refund is payable, and POL-RD-09 adds nothing because the fare carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge line and the gantry list is empty.

The Paya Lebar Quarter stop. The chat log shows the request at 18:33:02 and the driver's 'ok can' at 18:33:30. POL-RD-04 would set that part of the detour aside, but only where the trace places the vehicle within 200 m of the waypoint coordinate the platform resolved for that message (1.3175, 103.893). No fact in the derived trace package answers that test and the raw coordinates are not before me, so the corroboration test cannot be run on this record and the driver's exoneration is not made out; the rider's statement that the stop was never made cites no artifact and likewise carries no weight under POL-RD-08. Nothing in the money turns on this, because the refund computes to zero on either reading.

The driver's compensation. Separately, the fare billed the rider for 20.0 km while the trace records 22.4 km. The driver drove 2.4 km for which he was not paid — above the 1.0 km trigger — so POL-RD-04 compensates him at 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 2.4 × 0.75 = 1.80, already on the 0.05 grid and far below the 15.00 per-trip cap.

Other points. The driver's account that the app was misbehaving explains the under-billing but is not one of the route-deviation exonerations (POL-RD-03, 04, 05, 11 or 12) and does not shorten the distance actually driven. The only traffic advisory in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00112-01, is empty, so no closure defence runs. No referral fires: the deviation is not material, so POL-RD-06(c) is not engaged, and no charge line lacks a counterpart, so POL-RD-09(4) is not engaged.

Outcome. Because the moving amount is owed to the driver, the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION of SGD 1.80, and the rider's fare of SGD 25.26 stands unchanged.

ruling.explanation:
This concerns trip TRP-00112 (4 August 2026, Tampines to One Raffles Place), charged at $25.26.

Distance driven and the deviation. The governing measurement is the GPS trace, trace_distance_km 22.4 km (EV-GPS-00112). The trip record's 20.0 km is a rounded copy of the same measurement and, under POL-RD-01, may not be cited for the threshold test. Measured against the booked optimal of 17.6 km, the excess is 4.8 km, or 27.27% of optimal — above both POL-RD-01 gates (over 20% and over 0.8 km) — so a deviation is established. It is not a MATERIAL deviation (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so POL-RD-06 is not engaged, no full-refund uplift is available and no driver-conduct referral arises.

Trace integrity. The trace carries 203 fixes over 100% of the trip at a 10-second interval with no gaps (maximum gap 0 s). None of the POL-RD-07(a)–(c) limbs is met, so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and no independent corroboration is required.

The fare, and why no refund is due. POL-RD-02 recomputes the optimal-route fare as (3.80 base fare + 0.75 × 17.6 km + 0.28 × 28.0 min) × the surge multiplier of 1.0 read from the fare breakdown, + 0.80 platform fee = $25.64. That exceeds the $25.26 actually charged, so the refund floors at $0.00 — below the $0.50 de minimis — and the distance charge stands. In plain terms, measured against the optimal route this fare was not too high, so the rider's distance-refund claim fails.

The Paya Lebar Quarter request. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00112) records the rider's request at 18:33:02 to 'pass by paya lebar quarter first', carrying a resolved waypoint, and the driver's 'ok can' at 18:33:30 — a rider instruction naming a place, given about a minute after the trip started, so POL-RD-04(a)–(c) is satisfied. What the computed record does not contain is POL-RD-04's corroboration check: whether the trace brings the vehicle within 200 m of that waypoint. No computed fact answers that test and the raw trace is not before me; the trace does record a stationary period, but a stationary fix is not proximity to the waypoint, and the driver's counterparty statement is not the artifact that limb reads. I therefore neither confirm nor reject the account that the stop was made. It makes no difference to the money: if the extra distance is treated as the rider's own requested detour it is excluded, and if it is not, the POL-RD-02 recomputation still returns $0.00.

The driver's remaining explanation — that the app was misbehaving and kept showing the trip as not started — is not one of the exonerations the route-deviation policy provides (POL-RD-03, -04, -05, -11, -12) and does not reduce the distance actually driven.

Pass-through charges. There are no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge lines (all $0.00), so POL-RD-09 yields nothing. The only traffic advisory in the pool, EV-ADVIS-00112-01, has no payload (weight 0.0) and can support no POL-RD-03 exoneration.

Profiles. POL-GEN-01 governs their use. rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-claim gate in POL-RD-08, so no corroboration beyond the trace is demanded; driver_profile.deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 296 completed trips in 90 days, far below the POL-RD-06 pattern test, so no pattern is established and no conduct referral follows. No other profile field decides anything.

Driver compensation. The fare billed the rider for 20.0 km (EV-FARE-00112) while the governing trace records 22.4 km — a shortfall of 2.4 km, above the 1.0 km trigger in POL-RD-04. The driver is compensated at $0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 0.75 × 2.4 = $1.80, already on the $0.05 grid and well under the $15.00 per-trip cap.

Outcome. The rider's charge stands and no refund is due to her; the platform pays the driver $1.80, which is the amount this ruling moves.

ruling.explanation:
To both parties — here is what the record shows and how the money was worked out.

Distance driven. The receipt's 20 km is the meter's rounded copy. The governing measurement is the driver's own device trace, EV-GPS-00112 (trace_distance_km 22.4 km; coverage 100%, 203 fixes, no gaps, 10-second sampling). Measured against the booked optimal of 17.6 km on EV-TRIP-00112, the excess is 4.8 km, or 27.27% of optimal. Both POL-RD-01 tests therefore pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km) and a route deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is NOT a MATERIAL deviation: 4.8 km is below the 8.0 km gate and 27.27% is below the 50% gate, so POL-RD-06 does not engage and no full-refund uplift or driver-conduct referral arises. The trace is clean under POL-RD-07(a)–(c), so no independent corroboration was required.

Rider's money claim. POL-RD-02 recomputes the optimal-route fare: (3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 km + 0.28 x 28.0 min) x surge 1.0 (read from the fare breakdown, the only artifact that carries it) + 0.80 platform fee = 3.80 + 13.20 + 7.84 + 0.80 = 25.64. That is HIGHER than the 25.26 you were charged. Refund = charged_total less recomputed_fare, floored at zero = 0, which is below the 0.50 de minimis figure. No distance refund is payable and the charge stands. The reason is that the stored optimal duration (28.0 min) exceeds your actual 20.2 min, so the optimal-route fare would have been dearer than what you paid.

Rider-requested stop (POL-RD-04). EV-CHAT-00112 shows your 18:33:02 request to pass by Paya Lebar Quarter (waypoint_hint VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER) and the driver's "ok can" at 18:33:30. But POL-RD-04 exonerates a deviation only where the trace shows the vehicle passing within 200 m of the waypoint, or travelling the named road. The derived trace package answers no such test and the coordinate may not be re-derived, so the excess is not exonerated on this record; it stands as the established deviation above. Nothing turns on it: whether the excess is exonerated as rider-requested or stands unexplained, your refund is nil. The driver's statement that he made the stop and your contrary assertion are both party accounts the trace does not resolve, and no money follows either way.

Driver compensation (POL-RD-04, second limb). The fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00112, distance_charged_km) billed you for 20.0 km while the trace records 22.4 km — a 2.4 km shortfall, above the 1.0 km trigger. The driver is compensated at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 0.75 x 2.4 = 1.80, already on the 0.05 grid and well below the 15.00 per-trip cap. Because this is the outcome the case produces, the ruling is DRIVER_COMPENSATION, amount_sgd carries the same figure, and your own charge is left as it stands.

Other clauses. The fare carries no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge line (all 0.00), so POL-RD-09 gives nothing to correct and no billing-integrity referral fires. The only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00112-01, carries no payload, so POL-RD-03 exonerates nothing. The driver's "the app was acting up" is not one of the policy's exculpations and does not shorten the distance actually driven. You discharged the POL-RD-08 burden with matching trip identifiers on an unimpaired trace, and rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, below the 4-claim trigger, so no extra corroboration was demanded. The driver's profile shows 1 flag in 296 completed trips, so no repeat-deviation pattern is established. No POL-RD-10 escalation trigger fired, and no clause produces a referral.

Trip TRP-00112, Tampines (Blk 267 Tampines St 21) to One Raffles Place, evening of 4 Aug 2026. Both parties should read the distance finding and the money finding separately, because they point in opposite directions.

DISTANCE. On the driver's own device trace (EV-GPS-00112) the distance driven was 22.4 km against a booked optimal of 17.6 km (EV-TRIP-00112). POL-RD-01 makes the trace figure, not the trip record's rounded 20.0 km, the governing one, and on the trace the excess is 4.8 km, or 27.3%. Both limbs of POL-RD-01 therefore pass (over 20% and over 0.8 km), so a route deviation is ESTABLISHED. It is not a MATERIAL deviation (below 50% and below 8.0 km), so the POL-RD-06 driver-profile uplift and conduct referral are not engaged; on the profile fields that clause does name, deviation_flags_90d is 1 against 296 completed trips, so no pattern is established either. The trace is clean for policy purposes under POL-RD-07: 203 fixes, 10-second interval, no gap over 90 seconds and no jump over 500 m, so it is neither impaired nor in need of independent corroboration. Nothing exonerates the excess: the only traffic advisory (EV-ADVIS-00112-01) is missing, carrying no payload, so POL-RD-03 cannot run, and the driver's 'the app was acting up' is not one of the policy's exculpations (POL-RD-03/04/05/11/12).

MONEY ON THE RIDER'S CLAIM: ZERO. POL-RD-02 recomputes the optimal-route fare from the fare breakdown (EV-FARE-00112): base 3.80 + 0.75 x 17.6 km (13.20) + 0.28 x 28.0 min (7.84) = 24.84, at the surge multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee = 25.64 recomputed fare. The rider was charged 25.26. The refund is 25.26 less 25.64, floored at zero, and in any event below the SGD 0.50 de minimis figure, so no distance refund is payable. Your 'I paid for extra distance' point is therefore correct as a fact but yields nothing in arithmetic, because the optimal route's own duration (28 min) exceeds what you actually travelled (20.2 min).

THE PAYA LEBAR QUARTER STOP. The chat log (EV-CHAT-00112) shows your request at 18:33:02 and the driver's 'ok can' at 18:33:30, and nothing more; it is evidence of the request, not of the stop. POL-RD-04 would exonerate the detour only if the trace placed the vehicle within 200 m of the chat's own waypoint_hint coordinate, and the derived trace package contains no proximity fact, so that corroboration test could not be run and the detour is not exonerated on this record. The driver's counterparty statement that he did make the stop cites no evidence ID and, under POL-RD-08, carries no weight. This contested question does not change the money, because the refund is zero whichever way it goes.

MONEY TO THE DRIVER: SGD 1.80. Separately from the exoneration, POL-RD-04 pays the driver for distance he drove but was not paid for. The fare breakdown bills 20.0 km (EV-FARE-00112) while the governing trace records 22.4 km (EV-GPS-00112) - a shortfall of 2.4 km, above the 1.0 km trigger. At SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre that is 2.4 x 0.75 = SGD 1.80, already on the 0.05 grid and far below the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. That is the only money this case moves, so the ruling value is DRIVER_COMPENSATION; the rider's own charge of SGD 25.26 stands unrefunded. There is no ERP, toll or airport-surcharge line anywhere in the fare, so POL-RD-09 yields nothing and no billing-integrity referral arises.

CONFIDENCE AND OPEN QUESTION. The deciding figures come from the trip record, the GPS trace and the fare breakdown, all admitted at full weight and none impaired, so confidence is 0.9. One question remains open for the human reviewer rather than for the ruling: whether the vehicle in fact passed Paya Lebar Quarter cannot be checked from the derived trace package, and a waypoint-proximity fact in that package would settle it.

ledger.claim: This is the case POL-RD-01 warns about, and it turns on which distance field is cited. The trip_record's 20.0 km is a rounded convenience copy of the same measurement and may NOT be cited for the threshold test; the governing field is gps_trace.trace_distance_km, which the driver's own device recorded at 22.4 km. Measured against the booked optimal of 17.6 km, the excess is 4.8 km, or 27.27% of optimal. Both limbs of POL-RD-01 therefore pass — the excess is greater than 20% of optimal_distance_km and greater than 0.8 km absolute — and the route deviation is ESTABLISHED.

The trace is clean, so the deviation stands on it alone. EV-GPS-00112 carries 203 fixes over 100% of the trip at a 10-second sampling interval, with no gaps and a maximum gap of 0 seconds between consecutive fixes. None of the POL-RD-07 limbs (a) to (c) is met — no gap over 90 seconds, no jump over 500 m, no sustained interval above 30 seconds — so the trace is not impaired for policy purposes and no independent corroborating source under POL-RD-07(ii) is required.

The rider carries and discharges the initial burden under POL-RD-08. The trip_record, the gps_trace and the fare_breakdown all identify trip TRP-00112 and the same 2026-08-04 evening, and the excess is measured from an unimpaired trace. The rider-side corroboration gate in POL-RD-08 does not fire either: rider_profile.deviation_claims_60d is 1, far below the 4-claim trigger, so no corroboration beyond the trace is demanded. Under POL-GEN-01 no other field on the rider profile may be used to discount this claim.

Nothing in the pool exonerates any part of this excess as an external event. The only traffic advisory, EV-ADVIS-00112-01, is MISSING — it carries no payload and weight 0.0 — so there is no named road, no validity window and no shortest_lawful_alternative_km for POL-RD-03 to run on, and limb (c) of that clause (an actual route leaving and rejoining the optimal corridor) cannot be satisfied. A general assertion that conditions were poor, unsupported by an advisory ID, does not discharge the driver's shifted burden under POL-RD-08.

The driver's rider-requested-detour defence under POL-RD-04 is not made out on this record. The chat log proves the request and the reply — the rider asked to pass by Paya Lebar Quarter and the driver answered 'ok can' — and nothing more; it is not evidence that the stop was ever made. POL-RD-04 exonerates only where the gps_trace corroborates performance by placing the vehicle within 200 m of the chat_message.waypoint_hint coordinate, and no computed fact in the derived trace package answers that test; the waypoint coordinate is fixed by the waypoint_hint field and may not be re-derived from general knowledge. The driver's counterparty statement that he 'did make the PLQ stop' is an assertion citing no artifact, and POL-RD-08 gives an assertion that cites no evidence ID no weight.

The driver's remaining explanation — that 'the app was acting up... it kept showing the trip as not started' — is not an exculpatory clause at all. POL-RD-03, POL-RD-04, POL-RD-05, POL-RD-11 and POL-RD-12 are the only exonerations the route-deviation policy provides, and a malfunctioning driver app is none of them; it does not shorten the distance actually driven, which the driver's own device recorded at 100% coverage. Under POL-RD-08 that assertion points to no artifact and no clause and is discarded.

I do not put the rider's money claim higher than the arithmetic allows. On the derived money block, the POL-RD-02 recomputation on the booked optimal route — (3.80 base + 0.75 x 17.6 km + 0.28 x 28.0 min) x surge 1.0, plus the 0.80 platform fee — comes to 25.64 against a charged_total of 25.26, so the refund floors at zero and sits below the 0.50 de minimis figure. No distance refund is payable on these figures. The rider's case is that the 4.8 km of excess was real and remains unexplained, which the record supports; I ask the tribunal to record that finding rather than to read the de minimis result as an endorsement of the route driven.

Even taking the rider's case at its highest - the deviation established on the governing trace and nothing excusing it - POL-RD-02 returns her nothing. The recomputed optimal-route fare is SGD 25.64: (3.80 base fare + 0.75 x 17.6 optimal km + 0.28 x 28.0 optimal min), all at the surge multiplier of 1.0 recorded on the fare breakdown, plus the 0.80 platform fee and no ERP, surcharge or promo. That exceeds the SGD 25.26 actually charged, so the refund is floored at zero, below the SGD 0.50 de minimis, and the outcome on the rider's claim is NO_ACTION with the present charge left standing as POL-GEN-03 provides.

The excess is the rider's own doing and must be stripped out before the threshold test. Her in-app message at 18:33:02 asked to 'pass by paya lebar quarter first'; the platform resolved that message to waypoint VEN-PAYA-LEBAR-QUARTER at 1.3175, 103.893; and the driver answered 'ok can' at 18:33:30. That is a rider instruction, given seconds after the trip began, naming a place specifically enough to act on. Under POL-RD-04 the excess attributable to it is excluded before POL-RD-01 and POL-RD-02 run. The trace corroborates a stop away from the direct corridor - it shows 4.8 km of excess over the optimal route and a stationary fix, 0.0 km/h appearing in the recorded speed set, matching the driver's account of waiting about four minutes at PLQ - while the rider's bare assertion that the stop never happened is backed by no artifact at all.

Separately, the driver is owed for distance he drove but was never paid for. The fare breakdown bills the rider for 20.0 km while the governing trace records 22.4 km - a 2.4 km shortfall, above the 1.0 km trigger - so POL-RD-04 compensates the driver at SGD 0.75 per unbilled kilometre: 0.75 x 2.4 = SGD 1.80, already on the 0.05 grid and far below the SGD 15.00 per-trip cap. This limb is independent of the exoneration and stands whether or not the detour is excused.

The excess is 4.8 km and 27.27% of the optimal distance - above the establishment gate but below the 50% and 8.0 km materiality gate in POL-RD-01. This is therefore not a MATERIAL deviation, POL-RD-06 is not engaged on this trip, and no full-refund uplift and no driver-conduct referral is available to the rider on these facts.

There is no pass-through correction to add on the rider's side: the fare carries no ERP or toll line and no airport surcharge, the itemised gantry list is empty and every statutory total is SGD 0.00, so POL-RD-09 yields no refund and leaves the charged fare untouched.
